title: Could, would, should, can, might, have to, would rather
theme: Pedir com educação, dizer o que consegue, o que gostaria, o que deveria, o que talvez faça e o que precisa fazer
goal: Aluno sai usando "Could you...?", "May I...?", "I can / I can't", "I would love...", "I'd rather...", "You should...", "I might..." e "I have to / she has to" em situações de viagem.
module_chunks: Could you give me a glass of water?
May I go to the restroom?
I can go. / I can't go tonight.
I would love to eat this cake.
I would love to see the show.
There's no place I'd rather be.
I have to go to Central Park.

units.title: Could you...? May I...?
units.grammar_focus: Pedido educado com "Could you...?" e permissão com "May I...?"
units.real_life_context: No restaurante e no táxi você precisa pedir coisas com educação.

grammar.sentence: _____ you give me a glass of water, please?
grammar.explanation: "Could you...?" é o pedido mais educado: "você poderia...?". Dica do Igor: com "could" e "please", ninguém te acha grosso.

grammar.sentence: _____ I go to the restroom?
grammar.explanation: "May I...?" pede permissão: "posso...?". "May I go to the restroom?" = posso ir ao banheiro?

grammar.sentence: Could you _____ me to Central Park?
grammar.explanation: Depois de "could", verbo básico: "Could you take me to...?" = você poderia me levar até...?

grammar.sentence: Excuse me, may I _____ here?
grammar.explanation: "May I sit here?" = posso sentar aqui? Verbo básico depois de "may".

grammar.sentence: _____ you help me with my bag, please?
grammar.explanation: "Could you help me?" é mais educado; "Can you help me?" também funciona.

grammar.sentence: May I _____ a question?
grammar.explanation: "May I ask a question?" = posso fazer uma pergunta? Em inglês se "pergunta uma pergunta": "ask a question".

grammar.sentence: Could you speak more _____, please?
grammar.explanation: "Could you speak more slowly, please?" é a frase que salva quando o nativo fala rápido.

grammar.sentence: Could you to help me?
grammar.explanation: "Could" vai direto no verbo: "Could you help me?".

grammar.sentence: I may go to the restroom?
grammar.answer: May I go to the restroom?
grammar.explanation: Pergunta de permissão: "May I...?". A ordem muda como no "Can you...?".

grammar.passage: Igor: Excuse me, could you give me a glass of water? Waiter: Sure! Igor: And may I sit by the window? Waiter: Of course.
grammar.question: Onde o Igor quer sentar? (responda em inglês)
grammar.explanation: "May I sit by the window?" = posso sentar perto da janela? E o garçom respondeu "Of course" (claro).

listening_speaking.text: Could you give me a glass of water?
Excuse me, may I sit here, please?
Could you take me to Central Park?
May I go to the restroom, please?
Could you speak more slowly, please?

roleplay.scenario: Você entra num táxi em Nova York. O Igorfina faz o papel do taxista. Peça com educação.
roleplay.opening_line: Hey there! Where are we going today?

objectives.hidden_prompt: user politely asks to be taken somewhere: 'could you take me to...', 'can you take me to...', 'to Central Park, please' — must be in English
objectives.hint_pt: Could you take me to Central Park?
objectives.hint_en: Could you take me to Central Park?
examples_pass: Could you take me to Central Park?
Can you take me to the airport?

objectives.hidden_prompt: user asks permission or politely asks to open the window: 'may I open the window?', 'could you open the window?', 'can I open the window?' — must be in English
examples_pass: Could you open the window, please?

roleplay.closing_cue: Igorfina fecha com "Of course! Fresh air and the best driver in New York, ha!" quando obj_2 bater.
roleplay.suggested_flow:
**Suggested flow** (referencial, 4 turnos):

1. **Student**: ~"Could you take me to Central Park?"
2. **Igorfina**: "Sure thing! It's a bit hot today, huh?"
3. **Student**: ~"May I open the window?"
4. **Igorfina**: "Of course! Fresh air and the best driver in New York, ha!"

guided_chat.scenario: Você está num restaurante e o Igorfina é o garçom, atendendo pelo tablet da mesa.
guided_chat.intro_pt: Peça as coisas com educação usando Could you...? e May I...?
guided_chat.opening_message: Welcome! How can I help you today?

objectives.hidden_prompt: user politely asks for water: 'could you give me a glass of water?', 'could I have some water, please?' — must be in English
objectives.hint_pt: Could you give me a glass of water?
objectives.hint_en: Could you give me a glass of water?
examples_pass: Could you give me a glass of water?
Could I have some water, please?

objectives.hidden_prompt: user asks for the menu: 'could you bring the menu?', 'may I see the menu?', 'can I have the menu?' — must be in English
examples_pass: Could you bring me the menu?
Can I have the menu, please?

objectives.hidden_prompt: user thanks: 'thank you', 'thanks', 'thank you so much' — must be in English

guided_chat.closing_cue: Igorfina encerra com "You're welcome! The chef is ready when you are!" quando obj_3 bater.
guided_chat.suggested_script:
**Script** (referencial, 6 turnos):

1. **Igorfina**: "Welcome! How can I help you today?"
2. **Student**: "Could you give me a glass of water?"
3. **Igorfina**: "Sure! Anything else?"
4. **Student**: "May I see the menu?"
5. **Igorfina**: "Here you go. Today's special is lasagna."
6. **Student**: "Thank you so much!"
7. **Igorfina**: "You're welcome! The chef is ready when you are!"

units.title: I can, I can't
units.grammar_focus: Habilidade e possibilidade: I can / I can't / Can you...?
units.real_life_context: Um amigo te convida para várias coisas; você diz o que consegue e o que não dá.

grammar.sentence: I _____ go tonight, I'm free!
grammar.explanation: "I can go" = eu consigo ir / eu posso ir. "Can" não muda com a pessoa: I can, she can, they can.

grammar.sentence: Sorry, I _____ go tonight. I have to work.
grammar.explanation: "I can't go" = não consigo ir / não posso ir. "Can't" é a forma curta de "cannot".

grammar.sentence: _____ you swim?
grammar.explanation: Pergunta de habilidade: "Can you swim?" = você sabe nadar?

grammar.sentence: She can _____ English very well.
grammar.explanation: Depois de "can", verbo básico, mesmo com "she": "She can speak" (nunca "can speaks").

grammar.sentence: A: Can you drive? B: Yes, I _____.
grammar.explanation: Resposta curta: "Yes, I can" / "No, I can't".

grammar.sentence: I _____ find my phone! Can you call it?
grammar.explanation: "I can't find my phone" = não estou achando meu celular. Muito útil em viagem.

grammar.sentence: Can I _____ by card?
grammar.explanation: "Can I pay by card?" = posso pagar no cartão? Pergunta essencial no comércio.

grammar.sentence: I can to go tonight.
grammar.explanation: "Can" vai direto no verbo, sem "to".

grammar.sentence: He cans play the guitar.
grammar.explanation: "Can" é igual para todo mundo: "he can", nunca "he cans".

grammar.passage: Igor: Can you come to the beach tomorrow? Ana: I can't, I have to work. But I can go on Sunday! Igor: Perfect!
grammar.question: Quando a Ana pode ir? (responda em inglês)
grammar.explanation: "I can't" amanhã, mas "I can go on Sunday": no domingo.

listening_speaking.text: Yes! I can go with you tonight.
Sorry, I can't go. I have to work.
Can I pay by card, please?
I can't find my phone anywhere!
Can you swim? The beach is close.

roleplay.scenario: O Igorfina te convida para duas coisas no fim de semana. Diga o que dá e o que não dá.
roleplay.opening_line: Big weekend! Surfing on Saturday. Can you come?

objectives.label_pt: Dizer que não pode no sábado
objectives.hidden_prompt: user declines with can't: 'I can't', 'sorry, I can't go', 'I can't surf' — must be in English
user accepts with can: 'I can go on Sunday', 'yes, I can', 'I can go' — must be in English
examples_pass: I can go to the barbecue.

roleplay.closing_cue: Igorfina fecha com "Deal! Barbecue on Sunday, I'm the chef!" quando obj_2 bater.
roleplay.suggested_flow:
**Suggested flow** (referencial, 4 turnos):

1. **Student**: ~"Sorry, I can't go."
2. **Igorfina**: "No problem! Barbecue on Sunday?"
3. **Student**: ~"I can go on Sunday!"
4. **Igorfina**: "Deal! Barbecue on Sunday, I'm the chef!"

guided_chat.scenario: Na loja de aluguel de bicicletas, o Igorfina é o atendente pelo chat.
guided_chat.intro_pt: Você quer alugar uma bicicleta. Pergunte e responda com can.
guided_chat.opening_message: Hi! Bikes for rent. How can I help?

objectives.hidden_prompt: user asks with can: 'can I rent a bike?', 'can I get a bike for today?' — must be in English
examples_pass: Can I get a bike for today?

objectives.label_pt: Perguntar se pode pagar no cartão
objectives.hidden_prompt: user asks to pay by card: 'can I pay by card?', 'can I pay with a credit card?' — must be in English
examples_pass: Can I pay with my credit card?

objectives.label_pt: Responder se sabe andar de bike
objectives.hidden_prompt: user answers about ability with can: 'yes, I can', 'I can ride', 'I can't ride very well' — must be in English
examples_pass: I can't ride very well, ha.

guided_chat.closing_cue: Igorfina encerra com "Great! Helmet on and enjoy the park!" quando obj_3 bater.
guided_chat.suggested_script:
**Script** (referencial, 6 turnos):

1. **Igorfina**: "Hi! Bikes for rent. How can I help?"
2. **Student**: "Can I rent a bike?"
3. **Igorfina**: "Sure! Twenty bucks for the day."
4. **Student**: "Can I pay by card?"
5. **Igorfina**: "Yes. Quick question: can you ride well?"
6. **Student**: "Yes, I can!"
7. **Igorfina**: "Great! Helmet on and enjoy the park!"

units.title: I would love... I'd rather...
units.grammar_focus: Desejo e preferência: I would love to + verbo / I'd like + coisa / I'd rather + verbo
units.real_life_context: Num jantar de gala, o Igorfina imita um presidente exagerado oferecendo tudo "o melhor do mundo". Você diz o que gostaria e o que prefere.

grammar.sentence: I would love _____ eat this cake.
grammar.explanation: "I would love to + verbo" = eu adoraria... "I would love to eat this cake" = eu adoraria comer esse bolo.

grammar.sentence: I'd _____ have a soda, not a beer.
grammar.explanation: "I'd rather" = eu prefiro. "I'd rather have a soda" = prefiro um refrigerante. Depois de "rather", verbo básico.

grammar.sentence: There's no place I'd rather _____.
grammar.explanation: "There's no place I'd rather be" = não tem lugar onde eu preferiria estar. Frase de música e de discurso, ótima para elogiar um lugar.

grammar.sentence: I'd _____ a coffee, please.
grammar.explanation: "I'd like + coisa" = eu gostaria de... É o jeito educado de pedir no balcão.

grammar.sentence: I _____ love to see the show tonight!
grammar.explanation: "I would love to see the show" (ou "I'd love to"). Desejo educado e animado.

grammar.sentence: Tea or coffee? I'd rather _____ coffee.
grammar.explanation: "I'd rather have coffee" = prefiro café. Com comida e bebida, use "have".

grammar.sentence: Would you like some cake? Yes, I'd _____ to!
grammar.explanation: Resposta animada a um convite: "Yes, I'd love to!" = sim, eu adoraria!

grammar.sentence: I would love eat this cake.
grammar.answer: I would love to eat this cake.
grammar.explanation: Com "would love", vai "to" antes do verbo: "would love to eat".

grammar.sentence: I'd rather to have a soda.
grammar.explanation: "Would rather" é como "can": vai direto no verbo, sem "to".

grammar.passage: Igor (as the president): Folks, this cake is tremendous. The best cake. Would you like some? Guest: Yes, I'd love to! But I'd rather have a soda, not champagne.
grammar.question: O que o convidado prefere beber? (responda em inglês)
grammar.explanation: "I'd rather have a soda" = prefiro um refrigerante. E aceitou o bolo com "I'd love to!".

listening_speaking.text: I would love to eat this cake, thank you!
I'd rather have a soda, not a beer.
There's no place I'd rather be tonight.
I'd like a coffee with milk, please.
Yes, I'd love to see the show!

roleplay.scenario: Num jantar de gala, o Igorfina imita um presidente exagerado que te oferece "o melhor bolo do mundo" e "o melhor champanhe". Aceite o bolo e diga o que prefere beber.
roleplay.opening_line: Folks, welcome! This cake is tremendous, the best cake. Would you like some?

objectives.hidden_prompt: user accepts with would love/like: 'yes, I'd love to!', 'I would love to eat the cake', 'I'd love some' — must be in English
examples_pass: I would love to eat the cake.

objectives.hidden_prompt: user states a preference with would rather: 'I'd rather have a soda', 'I'd rather have water' — must be in English

roleplay.closing_cue: Igorfina fecha com "A soda! Tremendous choice. The best soda. Believe me!" quando obj_2 bater.
roleplay.suggested_flow:
**Suggested flow** (referencial, 4 turnos):

1. **Student**: ~"Yes, I'd love to!"
2. **Igorfina**: "Great! And champagne, the best champagne?"
3. **Student**: ~"I'd rather have a soda."
4. **Igorfina**: "A soda! Tremendous choice. The best soda. Believe me!"
evaluation_focus: "Would love to + verbo" e "would rather + verbo" (sem "to")

guided_chat.scenario: Você acabou de chegar à "festa incrível" do presidente (o Igorfina imitando), no terraço, e ela está acontecendo agora. Ele te recebe, oferece uma bebida e depois pizza ou sushi.
guided_chat.intro_pt: Você chegou à festa do 'presidente'. Diga o que adoraria, o que prefere e elogie o lugar.
guided_chat.opening_message: Welcome to my party, folks. The biggest party. Would you like a drink?

objectives.hidden_prompt: user accepts the offer with would love: 'I'd love one!', 'I'd love a drink!', 'yes, I would love to' — must be in English
user states a preference with would rather: 'I'd rather have pizza', 'I'd rather dance', 'I'd rather go early' — must be in English

user compliments the party using would rather or would love: 'there's no place I'd rather be!', 'I'd rather be here than at home!', 'I'd love to come back!' — must be in English and use 'd rather / would rather / 'd love / would love
objectives.hint_pt: There's no place I'd rather be!
objectives.hint_en: There's no place I'd rather be!
examples_pass: There's no place I'd rather be!
I'd rather be here than at home!
examples_fail: This place is amazing (no would rather/love)

guided_chat.closing_cue: Igorfina encerra com "Nobody says it better. Tremendous guest! Enjoy the party!" quando obj_3 bater.
guided_chat.suggested_script:
**Script** (referencial, 6 turnos):

1. **Igorfina**: "Welcome to my party, folks. The biggest party. Would you like a drink?"
2. **Student**: "I'd love a drink!"
3. **Igorfina**: "Tremendous. Pizza or sushi? Both are the best."
4. **Student**: "I'd rather have pizza."
5. **Igorfina**: "Great choice. And the view from the rooftop, incredible!"
6. **Student**: "There's no place I'd rather be!"
7. **Igorfina**: "Nobody says it better. Tremendous guest! Enjoy the party!"

units.title: You should... I might...
units.grammar_focus: Conselho com "should" e possibilidade com "might" (~70%) e "may" (~50%)
units.real_life_context: Um amigo te dá dicas da cidade e você diz o que talvez faça.

grammar.sentence: You _____ try the pizza in Brooklyn. It's amazing!
grammar.explanation: "You should" = você deveria. É conselho, dica. "You should try the pizza" = você deveria provar a pizza.

grammar.sentence: I _____ go to the beach tomorrow. I'm not sure.
grammar.explanation: "I might go" = talvez eu vá (~70% de chance, na escala do Igor). Usa quando não tem certeza.

grammar.sentence: Take an umbrella. It _____ rain today.
grammar.explanation: "It may rain" = pode ser que chova (~50%). "May" e "might" falam de possibilidade.

grammar.sentence: You should _____ this movie again. It's great!
grammar.explanation: Depois de "should", verbo básico: "You should watch this again".

grammar.sentence: You _____ visit the museum. It's free on Friday!
grammar.explanation: "You should visit the museum" = você deveria visitar o museu. Dica de amigo.

grammar.sentence: I'm tired. I _____ stay at the hotel tonight.
grammar.explanation: "I might stay at the hotel" = talvez eu fique no hotel.

grammar.sentence: A: Are you coming? B: I'm _____! 100%!
grammar.explanation: Na escala do Igor: "may" ~50%, "might" ~70%, "sure" 100%. "I'm sure!" = com certeza!

grammar.sentence: You should to try the pizza.
grammar.explanation: "Should" vai direto no verbo, igual a "can" e "could".

grammar.sentence: I might to go to the party.
grammar.answer: I might go to the party.
grammar.explanation: "Might" + verbo básico: "I might go".

grammar.passage: Igor: You should see the sunset at the Brooklyn Bridge. Ana: Good idea! I might go tomorrow. Igor: Take a jacket, it may get cold.
grammar.question: O que o Igor sugeriu levar? (responda em inglês)
grammar.explanation: "Take a jacket, it may get cold" = leve uma jaqueta, pode esfriar. Conselho (should), talvez (might) e possibilidade (may) na mesma conversa.

listening_speaking.text: You should try the pizza in Brooklyn.
I might go to the beach tomorrow.
Take an umbrella, it may rain today.
You should watch this movie again!
I'm sure, I'm going tonight!

roleplay.scenario: Você pede dicas da cidade para o Igorfina. Ele responde, e você diz o que talvez faça.
roleplay.opening_line: First time in Chicago? I have so many tips for you!

objectives.hidden_prompt: user asks for advice: 'what should I visit?', 'what should I do?', 'where should I go?' — must be in English
user states a possible plan with might/may: 'I might go tomorrow', 'I may visit it', 'I might do that' — must be in English
examples_pass: I may visit it on Sunday.

roleplay.closing_cue: Igorfina fecha com "You should! And take pictures for me, ha!" quando obj_2 bater.
roleplay.suggested_flow:
**Suggested flow** (referencial, 4 turnos):

1. **Student**: ~"What should I visit?"
2. **Igorfina**: "You should see the Bean in Millennium Park!"
3. **Student**: ~"I might go tomorrow."
4. **Igorfina**: "You should! And take pictures for me, ha!"

guided_chat.scenario: Um amigo seu vai viajar para Nova York e pergunta, pelo chat, o que fazer. Você é quem dá as dicas, e o Igorfina faz o papel do amigo.
guided_chat.intro_pt: Agora é você quem dá as dicas! Use You should... e responda o que talvez faça.
guided_chat.opening_message: Help! I'm going to New York next week. What should I do?

objectives.hidden_prompt: user gives advice with should: 'you should visit Central Park', 'you should try the pizza', 'you should take the ferry' — must be in English
user warns about a possibility with may/might: 'it may rain', 'it might be cold', 'it may snow' — must be in English
objectives.hint_pt: Take a jacket, it may be cold.
objectives.hint_en: Take a jacket, it may be cold.
examples_pass: Take a jacket, it may be cold.

objectives.label_en: Say if you might go too
objectives.hidden_prompt: user says whether they might join with might/may/sure: 'I might go with you', 'I may visit you', 'I might join you' — must be in English
examples_pass: I might join you next week.

guided_chat.closing_cue: Igorfina encerra com "That would be amazing! Best tour guide ever!" quando obj_3 bater.
guided_chat.suggested_script:
**Script** (referencial, 6 turnos):

1. **Igorfina**: "Help! I'm going to New York next week. What should I do?"
2. **Student**: "You should visit Central Park."
3. **Igorfina**: "Cool! Anything about the weather?"
4. **Student**: "Take a jacket, it may be cold."
5. **Igorfina**: "Good tip. Are you coming too?"
6. **Student**: "I might go with you!"
7. **Igorfina**: "That would be amazing! Best tour guide ever!"

---

units.title: I have to go! (e she has to)
units.grammar_focus: Obrigação: I have to / she has to / Do I have to...? + revisão do módulo
units.real_life_context: Você precisa ir embora de um encontro e explica o motivo; depois pergunta se precisa pagar uma taxa.

grammar.sentence: Sorry, I _____ to go. My bus leaves at six.
grammar.explanation: "I have to" = eu preciso / eu tenho que. "I have to go" é a frase clássica para sair de uma conversa.

grammar.sentence: She _____ to go to the airport now.
grammar.explanation: Com he/she/it, "have" vira "has": "She has to go". Dica do Igor: terceira pessoa, "has".

grammar.sentence: Do I _____ to pay for the museum?
grammar.explanation: "Do I have to pay?" = eu preciso pagar? Pergunta útil em museu, ônibus, praia.

grammar.sentence: I have to go to Central Park. Could you _____ me?
grammar.explanation: Frase do curso do Igor: "I have to go to Central Park. Could you take me?". Obrigação + pedido educado.

grammar.sentence: He _____ to work tomorrow, so he can't come.
grammar.explanation: "He has to work" = ele precisa trabalhar. "Has" com he/she/it.

grammar.sentence: You don't _____ to pay. It's free!
grammar.explanation: "You don't have to pay" = você não precisa pagar. Atenção: "don't have to" é "não precisa", não é "não pode".

grammar.sentence: Sorry, I have to _____. See you tomorrow!
grammar.explanation: "I have to go" = preciso ir. Despedida educada.

grammar.sentence: She have to go now.
grammar.explanation: "She has to", nunca "she have to".

grammar.sentence: I have go to the hotel.
grammar.answer: I have to go to the hotel.
grammar.explanation: A obrigação é "have to + verbo". Sem o "to", vira outra coisa.

grammar.passage: Igor: I have to go, my show starts at eight. Ana has to go too, her flight is at ten. Could you call us a taxi?
grammar.question: Por que a Ana precisa ir? (responda em inglês)
grammar.explanation: "Her flight is at ten": o voo dela é às dez. Repare: "I have to" com o Igor e "Ana has to" com a Ana.

listening_speaking.text: Sorry, I have to go. My bus is here.
She has to go to the airport now.
Do I have to pay for the museum?
You don't have to pay, it's free today.
I have to go to Central Park. Could you take me?

roleplay.scenario: Você está no museu e não sabe se precisa pagar. O Igorfina faz o papel do funcionário.
roleplay.opening_line: Welcome to the museum! How can I help you?

objectives.label_en: Ask if you have to pay
objectives.hidden_prompt: user asks with have to: 'do I have to pay?', 'do I have to buy a ticket?' — must be in English
examples_pass: Do I have to buy a ticket?
Do we have to pay to enter?

objectives.hidden_prompt: user politely asks for a map: 'could you give me a map?', 'may I have a map?', 'can I get a map, please?' — must be in English
objectives.hint_pt: Could you give me a map?
objectives.hint_en: Could you give me a map?
examples_pass: Could you give me a map?
May I have a map, please?

objectives.label_en: Say you have to leave at 5
objectives.hidden_prompt: user states an obligation with have to: 'I have to leave at five', 'I have to go at five' — must be in English
objectives.hint_pt: I have to leave at five.
objectives.hint_en: I have to leave at five.
examples_pass: I have to leave at five.
I have to go at five o'clock.
I have to be at the hotel at five.

roleplay.closing_cue: Igorfina fecha com "No problem! The best part is on the second floor, go there first!" quando obj_3 bater.
roleplay.suggested_flow:
**Suggested flow** (referencial, 6 turnos):

1. **Student**: ~"Do I have to pay?"
2. **Igorfina**: "No, it's free today!"
3. **Student**: ~"Could you give me a map?"
4. **Igorfina**: "Here you go. How much time do you have?"
5. **Student**: ~"I have to leave at five."
6. **Igorfina**: "No problem! The best part is on the second floor, go there first!"
evaluation_focus: "Have to" para obrigação e "Do I have to...?" para perguntar

guided_chat.scenario: O Igorfina organiza um passeio do grupo e quer saber quem pode ir. Responda com o que você e uma amiga precisam fazer.
guided_chat.intro_pt: O Igorfina está montando o passeio. Use have to e has to.
guided_chat.opening_message: Boat tour tomorrow at nine! Who's in?

objectives.label_pt: Dizer o que você precisa fazer
objectives.label_en: Say what you have to do
objectives.hidden_prompt: user states own obligation with have to: 'I have to work in the morning', 'I have to check out at ten' — must be in English
objectives.hint_pt: I have to work in the morning.
objectives.hint_en: I have to work in the morning.
examples_pass: I have to work in the morning.
I have to check out at ten.
I have to call my boss.

objectives.hidden_prompt: user states a third-person obligation with HAS to: 'Ana has to go to the airport', 'she has to work' — must be in English
objectives.hint_pt: Ana has to go to the airport.
